title: Economic development partnership renewal and municipal sponsorship strategy
subtitle: Rossford Crescent budget, water financial plan, weather standards, building by-law update and a new planning position
overview: The Finance and Corporate Services Committee recommended renewing the City's partnership agreement with the Waterloo Region Economic Development Corporation, which leads business attraction for the region. The new agreement raises municipal funding after years of flat contributions. The committee also recommended an updated municipal sponsorship strategy {{vote:m6}}, which sends sponsorship revenue to the business unit or asset being sponsored.

Consent items covered infrastructure and regulation. The committee recommended a $400,000 budget increase for the Rossford Crescent reconstruction, approval of the water distribution financial plan, delegated authority for significant weather event declarations under provincial minimum maintenance standards, and a rewritten Building by-law. The by-law update includes a new planning position funded by the Building Enterprise, not by property taxes. A councillor pulled that item for discussion, and it was recommended {{vote:m4}}.
These are recommendations. Council will consider them at a later meeting. Staff also agreed to circulate a list of City assets not currently offered for sponsorship before the next Council meeting.

decisions.detail: The committee recommended approving the new Waterloo Region Economic Development Corporation partnership agreement and its funding, and authorizing the Mayor and Clerk to sign it subject to the City Solicitor's satisfaction.
The committee recommended approving the amended sponsorship strategy, the revised revenue allocation in the sponsorship policy, and the updated sponsorship asset inventory.

The committee recommended repealing and replacing Chapter 710 (Building) of the Municipal Code and having the Building Enterprise fund one new full-time planning position to support zoning compliance.
The committee recommended increasing the project budget by $400,000 from the Water Infrastructure Program and extending the AECOM purchase order by $228,500.
The committee recommended approving the Kitchener Water Distribution System financial plan, which shows the system's financial viability under provincial drinking water regulations.
The committee recommended that Council delegate authority for significant weather event declarations and adopt Ontario Regulation 239/02 as the minimum maintenance standards through a by-law.

debate: On the building position, one councillor asked why a new full-time position was not left for the budget process. Staff said it responds to provincial legislative changes (Bill 23) and that the industry liaison committee raised no objection. Staff added that building permit fees fund it, not taxes.

On the economic development agreement, councillors asked about communications. The Mayor asked the corporation to better reflect Kitchener and all seven municipalities in its regional branding, and the corporation's representative agreed.

Equity of funding was raised. One councillor noted the cities and the region carry most of the cost while the townships' contributions stay flat. The corporation said townships have little economic development capacity and that one large investment skews the results.

The corporation's representative said inflation-linked increases came only in the last two years of the agreement and called the earlier omission an oversight. Councillors also asked about federal and provincial funding, which is not yet confirmed. The corporation also cited encampments as a concern raised by some prospective investors.

On sponsorship, some councillors wanted dedicated staff and a stronger public-facing platform to promote opportunities and past successes. Staff favoured relationship-based outreach led by one coordinating staff member. One councillor said they might bring a business case or amendment to Council.
